title: Molar Mass
short: Add up the atomic masses in a formula to get the mass of one mole in grams.
trouble: Students forget to multiply by a subscript, or by the 2 outside the parentheses in Ca(NO₃)₂.

blocks.html: The Mole gave the mass of one mole of atoms. Compounds work the same way: a mole of molecules (or formula units) has a mass equal to the sum of its atoms' masses. Reading the formula correctly, including the parentheses of polyatomic ions, is the whole skill.

The molar mass of a substance (g/mol) is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in its formula, each multiplied by how many times it appears. $$M(\mathrm{H_2O}) = 2(1.01) + 16.00 = 18.02\ \text{g/mol}.$$

One mole of $\mathrm{H_2O}$ molecules contains 2 mol of H atoms and 1 mol of O atoms. Their masses are $2 \times 1.01\ \text{g}$ and $16.00\ \text{g}$, so the mole of water weighs their sum. A subscript after parentheses multiplies everything inside: $\mathrm{Ca(NO_3)_2}$ contains 1 Ca, 2 N and 6 O.

blocks.title: Glucose
blocks.q: Find the molar mass of glucose, $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}$ (C 12.01, H 1.01, O 16.00).

blocks.title: Parentheses
blocks.q: Find the molar mass of calcium nitrate, $\mathrm{Ca(NO_3)_2}$ (Ca 40.08, N 14.01, O 16.00).

blocks.title: A hydrate
blocks.q: Find the molar mass of copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate, $\mathrm{CuSO_4\cdot 5H_2O}$ (Cu 63.55, S 32.07, O 16.00, H 1.01).
steps: The dot means each formula unit carries 5 water molecules: count them in.

blocks.html: For ionic compounds, which have no molecules, the same sum is sometimes called the formula mass. It is still the mass of one mole of formula units, in g/mol.

Forgetting to multiply by a subscript, or by the 2 outside the parentheses in $\mathrm{Ca(NO_3)_2}$ (giving 102.09 instead of 164.10). Before adding anything, write out how many of each atom the formula holds; the counts should match the formula exactly.
